Both flagged original-resolution screenshots show prose and no diagram.

diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and original final Remark specify boxes 1=(1,1), 2=(2,1), 3=(2,2). Figure has one box in row 1 and two in row 2, numbered down columns. Hence p=(1,2), q=(2,1), and box 3 is the rightmost lower box.

For the natural module matrix-unit action Eij(vk)=delta(j,k)vi (also used in supplier def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors step 1.1), e=E23 maps v3 to v2 and kills v1,v2. Arrow starts at box 3 and terminates at box 2. Its label and caption identify e, not x1.

With c=(0,0), q=(2,1), n=2, a1=0+2-2=0 and a2=0+1-2=-1. The figure places these above the first and second columns. Combining these diagonal actions with e gives x1v1=x1v2=0 and x1v3=v2-v3, exactly proof step 1.1.

For av1+bv2+cv3, x1 acts as c(v2-v3), so its kernel is Cv1 direct-sum Cv2. Adding the identity gives av1+(b+c)v2, whose kernel is C(v3-v2). This checks the caption and ensures the figure never presents v3 itself as a -1 eigenvector.

The distinct displayed diagonal column scalars are 0 and -1. The caption refers to the existing proved eigenspaces and does not use the diagram to establish the all-degree minimal-polynomial claim; the original proof remains unchanged.
